After the webshop receives the order, several things happen at the same time: the webshop sends an invoice, delivers the order, and updates its inventory. Once all these activities are complete, the manufacturer receives the order and starts building.

After the manufacturer starts building, a check is performed to see if the stock is greater than 5. If it is, the project is finished, and the process ends. If the stock is not greater than 5, a check is made to see if the stock is equal to 0. If it is, a compliment email is written, and then the project is finished, and the process ends.

If the stock is not equal to 0, it is checked if the stock is less than 3. If it is, the part with the faster delivery is ordered, the webshop receives this order, and the parallel activities (sending an invoice, delivering the order, updating inventory) and the subsequent manufacturing process are repeated. If the stock is not less than 3, it is then checked if it's less than 5. If it is, the cheapest part is ordered, the order is made to the webshop, and the process continues as before from making the order. If the stock is not less than 5, the project is finished, and the process concludes.

Based on the analysis, the manufacturer orders the necessary parts from suppliers and waits to receive them. If not all parts are received, the manufacturer checks with the suppliers and waits again for the parts. This cycle continues until a decision is made that all parts have been received.

Once all parts are in hand, they undergo a manual inspection. Following the inspection, the chainsaw is assembled, and the customer receives regular updates during this stage. If no improvements are required, the manufacturer proceeds to simultaneously produce the rest of the order and monitor the progress, sending regular updates to the customer throughout the monitoring. Once both production and monitoring are complete, the complete order is sent to the customer. The manufacturer's process ends at this point. The customer's process concludes upon receiving the complete order.

The process involves three participants: a Company, a Job Seeker, and a Job Plattform.

The process for the Job Seeker begins by reporting their application status, which is sent to the Job Plattform for analysis. The Job Seeker then goes through job offers received from the Job Plattform and proceeds to apply for a suitable one. This application is sent to the Job Plattform. A decision is then made; if the application is declined, the Job Seeker reports their application status again. If the application is accepted, the Job Seeker enters a probation phase, after which they rate the company. This rating is sent to the Job Plattform. If the company is rated C or less, the Job Seeker goes back to browsing job offers. If the company is rated higher than C, the Job Seeker has a permanent job, and their part of the process ends with having found a job.

The process for the Company starts upon receiving a job application from the Job Plattform. The company then simultaneously confirms the job application and rates the job application. Both the confirmation and the rating are sent to the Job Plattform. A decision is made based on the outcome. If the application is declined, the process ends with no employee being found. If it is accepted, the company negotiates an interview and then rates the job seeker. This rating is sent to the Job Plattform. Another decision is made: if the outcome is declined, the process ends with no employee found. If accepted, the company hires the prospective customer, and the process concludes with an employee being found.

The Job Plattform's process begins by sending job offers to the Job Seeker. It then analyses reports received from the Job Seeker and forwards the application to the Company. Following this, the platform receives both the job confirmation and the application rating from the Company. If the application is declined, the platform sends out new job offers. If it is accepted, the platform then receives the seeker rating from the Company and the company rating from the Job Seeker. A final decision is made: if declined, new job offers are sent. If the company rating is greater than C and the seeker has been accepted, the process ends with the job being conveyed.

The user starts by entering the manufacturer, the model, and then the broken part into an online tool. If the entered information is not correct, the user can re-enter the broken part. Once the information is accepted, the online tool simultaneously computes the parts list and the necessary tools. After both lists are generated, the user checks them against their own inventory of tools and screws.

If the user has everything needed, the online tool proceeds to generate the instructions to fix the phone. However, if the user is missing items, a decision is made whether to contact a friend. If they choose to contact a friend, they do so before getting everything else needed. If they decide not to contact a friend, they proceed directly to getting everything else needed. After all necessary items are acquired, the online tool generates the instructions to fix the phone.

The user then follows the instructions. After each step, a check is performed to see if there is another step in the instruction. If there is, the user follows the next instruction, continuing this loop until all steps are completed. Once there are no more steps, the user checks if the phone is working now.

If the phone is not working, the user sends the phone to an expert, and the process concludes with the phone being repaired.

If the phone is working, the user leaves a review. They are then asked if they want to upload a video of the repair. If they choose to upload a video, they do so, and the online tool saves the video to its database, after which the process ends with the phone being repaired. If the user decides not to upload a video, the process simply ends with the phone being repaired.

This process involves three participants: a Manufacturer, an Artist, and a 3D Printer.

The process is initiated by the Manufacturer, who sends sketches and further information to the Artist. Simultaneously, the Manufacturer waits to receive an STL file and also chooses a plastic color.

Upon receiving the information, the Artist creates a project and generates an STL file. The Artist then sends this STL file to the Manufacturer, concluding their part of the process.

After the Manufacturer chooses a color, a check is performed to see if the color is in stock. If it's not, the color is ordered. In either case, the next step is to check how much of the color is left. If less than 100g is available, the color is ordered. This file is then sent to the 3D printer, which concludes the Manufacturer's part of the process.

A check is performed to see if the printer is heated up. If it is not, it continues the heating process. Once it is heated up, it prints the object. When the object is printed, the process ends.

The user's process begins with creating an account and specifying basic information. Following this, one or more actions can be taken: the user may need a bank account, provide residence information, and provide job information.

If the user needs a bank account, they browse bank account offers and then apply for one. If the bank account application is accepted, they upload the form and attach the bank approval, and the process concludes with the bank account being uploaded. If the application is not accepted, they return to apply for a bank account again.

If the user needs to provide residence information, they provide the data of their Austrian residence. A check is then made to see if they have a residence. If they do, they can proceed. If they do not, they must make a plan on how to get an apartment. To get an apartment, they can either choose to use the provided tool or try to get an apartment on their own. If they use the tool, they browse open apartments and then conduct a virtual round-tour with the landlord. After the tour, a check for mutual interest in renting is made. If there is mutual interest, a contract is signed. If not, the process returns to making a plan on how to get an apartment. If they try on their own, a check is performed to see if it worked out. If it did, they proceed. If it did not, they return to making a plan on how to get an apartment. Once a contract is signed or it is confirmed they have a residence, an apartment contract is uploaded.

If the user needs to provide job information, they provide information for their job or venture. A check is then performed to see if it fits the RWR card regulations. If it does, a work contract and insurance documents are uploaded. If it does not, a digital CV is created and a list of open positions is browsed simultaneously. After both are done, the user can send an application. A check is then made to see if they receive an invite. If they do, they attend a job interview. If not, they can send another application. After the interview, a check for mutual interest in cooperation is made. If there is mutual interest, the contract is negotiated. If not, the user can send another application again. After negotiation, if an agreement is reached, a work contract and insurance documents are uploaded. If no agreement is reached, the user can once again send a new application.

After either the apartment contract or the work contract and insurance documents are uploaded, a reapplication for the RWR card is sent. The user then waits for a message. Upon receiving it, a timer for 2 years until renewal starts. After the two years, the user decides about their future. A check is then made to see if they want to renew. If they do, the process repeats from the point of providing residence and job information. If they do not, the process ends because the RWR card is now irrelevant. If at any point after receiving the message the user decides not to wait for the renewal period, the process can also end with no success.

The process starts in the Farming Bot Game when the Player has a desire to create a farming bot. First, the player finds out the wanted resources. This is followed by two parallel actions: the player collects the urgently needed resources while also checking the repository for already available resources. After these are done, a decision is made based on whether new tools are needed. If they are, the player builds the tools. Regardless, the player then collects the remaining resources.

Once the resources are collected, the Farming Bot takes over and simultaneously updates its list of resources while also beginning to wait for a random natural event for some time. A decision is made based on whether a random natural event happened. If it did, the bot is reset, and then the bot will either start farming or continue farming. If a random natural event did not happen, the bot will immediately start farming.

After starting or continuing to farm, the bot checks if a new milestone has been achieved. If no milestone has been achieved, the bot makes a decision on whether it has finished. If it has not finished, it gives itself a sleeping break before once again waiting for a random natural event. If a new milestone was achieved, the player is notified and reads the message. After reading, the bot checks if it has finished.

If the bot has finished, the player can choose to brag to friends, help with materials, or both. After either or both of these actions, the list of resources is updated by the bot, and the process ends.
